html:
Cooper Creek is a river of inland Australia. It forms in southwest Queensland where the Thomson and Barcoo rivers meet, and runs southwest through the flat, braided Channel Country into South Australia, toward Lake Eyre. Most years it dries to a chain of waterholes; only in big floods does it reach the lake.

Its deep waterholes made it a lifeline in the desert. Aboriginal peoples lived along it for many thousands of years, fishing, hunting and grinding the seeds of nardoo, a water fern, for flour. They included the Yandruwandha and Yawarawarka on the lower creek, the Birria near its source, the Dieri around its delta and the Pilatapa to the south.

The creek is best known for the Burke and Wills expedition. In 1860 and 1861 the explorers set up a depot there on their way to the Gulf of Carpentaria. On their return the depot party had left that same day, and Burke and Wills died by the creek. The one survivor, John King, lived because Yandruwandha people fed him. Cattle stations and, later, gas fields followed.
